identity.name: Phosphated distarch phosphate
identity.chemical_class: Chemically modified starch (phosphate-esterified and cross-linked distarch phosphate)

function.mechanism: Produced by esterification/cross-linking of native starch with phosphorus-containing compounds; phosphorylation and chain cross-linking modify hydration, viscosity, and processing stability.
common_food_categories: Foods using food starch-modified under GMP/technical need
Starch-thickened processed foods (e.g., sauces and texture-modified foods)

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 modified-starch re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: Published re-evaluation for E1413 within modified starches found no safety concern at reported uses and no numerical ADI required.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (INS 1413); 2018 entry was specification-only update.

concerns.summary: Older rodent studies on related modified distarch phosphates reported mineral-metabolism and nephrocalcinosis-type findings under high dietary inclusion; relevance to current E1413 exposures is uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation for modified starches reported no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.
Modified starches were considered not of genotoxic concern in EFSA's assessment.
No numerical ADI was considered necessary by EFSA, consistent with prior ADI 'not specified' positions.

populations: High consumers in the general population (group exposure assessed by EFSA)
adi_exceedance.notes: Classical ADI exceedance assessment is not applicable because EFSA/JECFA did not establish a numerical ADI for this modified-starch group.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations (EFSA/JECFA) are broadly reassuring and U.S. authorization exists, but evidence is largely group-based/read-across and recent E1413-specific toxicology is sparse.
key_factors: EFSA published re-evaluation with no safety concern and no numerical ADI requirement
JECFA ADI not specified for INS 1413
Authorized under 21 CFR 172.892 as food starch-modified
No IARC carcinogenic group classification identified
Older animal findings on related modified starches introduce limited residual uncertainty
